svg.title: Shielded VM startup and key-release sequence
svg.desc: Read eight numbered steps from top to bottom. The guarded host collects evidence. HGS Attestation evaluates policy and issues a health certificate. The host presents the certificate and VM key protector to Key Protection Service. KPS checks both host evidence and VM authorization, then returns key material encrypted to host VBS. The protected environment enables the vTPM, and the guest uses it to unlock its BitLocker OS volume. Passing attestation alone does not authorize every VM.
svg.text: Startup: two authorization decisions before unlock
Read from top to bottom. Arrows connect stages, not administrator permissions.

g.text: 1. Guarded host collects evidence
TPM identity, measured boot, and code integrity state.
Evidence must represent the actual approved host configuration.
2. HGS Attestation evaluates host policy
Identity and security evidence must satisfy the active attestation mode.
An unapproved host is rejected at this decision.
3. HGS issues a health certificate
The certificate provides limited-validity evidence of host acceptance.
It is not permission to unlock every VM.
4. Host requests this VM's protected key material
The request includes the health certificate and VM key protector (KP).
The KP identifies authorized guardian keys.
5. Key Protection Service checks VM authorization
KPS validates the certificate and whether its keys can serve this KP.
A healthy host can still be denied this particular VM.
6. KPS returns material protected for host VBS
Released material is encrypted for the host's isolated environment.
HTTPS transport does not replace this authorization or protection.
7. Protected host components enable the vTPM
The VM's existing protected state and KP must remain consistent.
The physical host TPM and guest vTPM have different identities.
8. Guest BitLocker unlocks the OS volume
Guest policy uses the vTPM to support release of the volume key.
The owner separately verifies guest access and data-volume protection.

svg.text: Periodic attestation is not continuous guest monitoring or instant revocation.
